preamble: Coda lenition turns a syllable-final voiceless bilabial stop [p] into the voiceless velar fricative [x]: the stop closure is released into frication and the place of articulation is lost to the dorsal default. Sakhalin Ainu is the documented case. Where Hokkaido Ainu keeps syllable-final /p/, /t/, /k/ and /r/, Sakhalin Ainu lenited these codas and merged them into a single phoneme /x/, written with small katakana h (ㇵ, ㇸ, ㇷ, ㇹ) and transliterated h; after /i/ it is realized [ç]. Hokkaido cup 'sun, moon' and cep 'fish' correspond to Sakhalin cuh and ceh. The change is confined to one dialect group of the Ainu family, so it is rare.

examples.from: Hokkaido Ainu cup [cúp] 'sun, moon, month' (retains the stop)
examples.note: Hattori's dialect survey, reproduced on Wiktionary, gives cúp for Yakumo, Horobetsu, Saru, Obihiro and Asahikawa against Karafuto (Sakhalin) cuh.
Wiktionary lists cep as the Hokkaido and Kuril form and ceh as the Sakhalin form.
